title: Three Terms and One Short Ruler
subtitle: 困难与应对 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 困难与应对（做人与做事·困难与应对）
meta: 主题语境：困难与应对（做人与做事·困难与应对）　|　核心词汇：mistake　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 mistake 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1966 the teacher ① made the mistake that no pupil in the classroom would have measured, and he said the making was the whole of the term. The ② mistake, meaning the slip itself and not the ruler, ran three terms and stayed unmeasured in the book; a mistake, he said, is the only thing in a classroom that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ mistake in that classroom had the same short ruler beside it, and the ④ mistake at the far blackboard, meaning the page they kept for the children to copy and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A mistake, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the teacher said the measuring is the part that fills three terms.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the mistake was the whole of the matter, meaning the lesson and not the slip. The ⑥ mistake, meaning the lesson and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; mistake, he said, is either something you make or the only word that means both a slip and a lesson. He said the lesson is the part they remember.

By 1971 the ⑦ mistake had become a line in a notebook, and the notebook had become an argument about the short ruler. The ⑧ mistake of the whole thing, the teacher wrote in March, was one classroom and three terms of measuring; mistake, he said, is either the page at the far blackboard or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ mistake I remember is the slip measured in the notebook, which closed in 1973 and is still measured as the quietest in the classroom. A ⑩ mistake, my mother said in 1975, is the only slip that improves by being measured; every mistake, she said, is a lesson that has agreed to look like a slip. She said the lesson was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 错误；失误（指教室里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 错误；失误（指那个错误本身，与短短的尺子相对）
C. 固定搭配：make the mistake 犯这一个错误
D. n. 错误；失误（指留给孩子们照着抄的那一页）
E. n. 错误之事（抽象总称，指一处教室的错误之事）
F. n. 错误；失误（指笔记簿里写到、被测量的那一个）
G. n. 错误、教训（指一件事里人人都学却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 教训（抽象总称，指人人都学却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: made the mistake that no pupil in the classroom would have measured
The mistake, meaning the slip itself and not the ruler
the mistake at the far blackboard
the mistake was the whole of the matter
the mistake had become a line in a notebook
The mistake of the whole thing
A mistake, my mother said in 1975

answers.why: make the mistake 意为“犯这一个错误”，1966 年那位先生把教室里没有一位学童肯测量的一个错误做了一遍。
mistake 意为“错误；失误”，指那个错误本身而不是短短的尺子，它经过了三个学期而在簿子上没有被测量。
mistake 意为“错误；失误”，指教室里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一把短短的尺子。
mistake 意为“错误；失误”，指最远那块黑板的留给孩子们照着抄的那一页，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
mistake 意为“错误、教训”，指一件事里人人都学却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个教训就是那件事的全部。
mistake 意为“教训”，指人人都学却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个错误，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
mistake 意为“错误；失误”，指笔记簿里写到、被测量的那一个，到 1971 年这一个成了笔记簿里的一行。
mistake 意为“错误之事”，先生三月写道，整件事的错误之事是一处教室和三个学期的测量。
mistake 意为“错误；失误”，我记得的是笔记簿里测量过的那一个，1973 年教完了，至今仍被说成教室里最安静的一个。
mistake 为抽象总称，母亲 1975 年说，错误是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的错误。
